papers.title: Characterizing transition state in mouse vigilance with electroencephalogram-electromyogram hypnodensity.
papers.summary: This study characterized vigilance-state transitions in mice using EEG/EMG and validated SVM classifiers trained on stable-state features to predict transition midpoints, revealing distinct transition dynamics such as longer NREMS-to-REMS transitions and abrupt REMS-to-NREMS transitions.

papers.title: Diurnal time and sleep pressure modulate cerebrospinal fluid low-frequency oscillations in synchrony with wake-promoting nuclei
papers.summary: In a 34-hour sleep deprivation study with fMRI/EEG and NIRS, CSF low-frequency oscillations increased with time awake and exhibited diurnal fluctuations, peaking in early morning, and were associated with vigilance and reticular activating system activity but not plasma norepinephrine.

papers.title: REM Sleep Disengagement of β Oscillations Permits Rapid Dream Movements in Parkinsonism
papers.summary: In non-human primates, MPTP-induced parkinsonism enhanced beta oscillations and impaired movement-related neural dynamics during wake and NREM sleep, but these were attenuated during REM sleep, with beta suppression preceding REM onset, suggesting brain-state gating of parkinsonian dysfunction.

papers.title: Meta-Analysis of Face-Validity Indicators in Automatically Detected Dog Sleep Spindles.
papers.summary: This meta-analysis evaluated automatic sleep spindle detection in dogs against three face validity criteria from human EEG, finding that most datasets met the criteria, supporting the dog as a model for sleep spindle research.

papers.title: Automated autism spectrum disorder detection using EEG signals and time-frequency visibility graphs.
papers.summary: This study proposed an EEG-based ASD detection framework combining time-frequency analysis and Horizontal Visibility Graphs, achieving 93.54% accuracy with DWT-HVG and Soft Voting Ensemble, outperforming other methods.

papers.title: Fully-automated sleep staging for Parkinson's disease and isolated REM sleep behavior disorder.
papers.summary: This study adapted and finetuned the U-Sleep deep neural network for automated sleep staging in Parkinson's disease and isolated REM sleep behavior disorder, achieving human-level agreement (κ=0.64) on a clinical hold-out. Confidence-based thresholds improved REM detection precision from 85% to 95.6%, enabling scalable and standardized PSG analysis.

papers.title: Leednet: a lightweight network for event detection in EEG signals.
papers.summary: The paper presents LEEDNet, a lightweight convolutional network for EEG event detection, achieving 81.2% accuracy and 77.5% macro-F1 on the NMT-Events dataset with only 0.25M parameters. Raw EEG input performed best compared to FFT and wavelet features, and a 2-second decision window was optimal.

papers.title: Chronic corticosterone exposure disrupts bile acids homeostasis associated with circadian dysfunction in the liver of chickens.
papers.summary: This study in chickens found that chronic corticosterone exposure disrupted hepatic circadian clock genes and bile acid metabolism, altering diurnal rhythms and phase relationships. Glucocorticoids also enhanced MRP2-mediated bile acid efflux in vitro, linking stress to enterohepatic bile acid remodeling.

papers.title: Respiratory phase shapes brain-heart dynamics: evidence from recurrence analysis of EEG band power and heart rate.
papers.summary: This study in 15 healthy subjects showed that inhale-hold periods during controlled breathing increased gamma band power, heart rate, and recurrence rate, while exhale-hold decreased these measures. The findings suggest respiratory phase modulates brain-heart dynamics, potentially reflecting distinct autonomic states.

papers.title: DTI-ALPS as a marker of glymphatic function: Review of the literature findings, methodology, and interpretation.
papers.summary: This review summarizes the DTI-ALPS technique as a non-invasive MRI marker of glymphatic function, finding 393 articles with applications in neurodegenerative and other disorders. Despite methodological variations, DTI-ALPS is a sensitive but non-specific marker of white matter microstructural damage and neuroinflammation.

papers.title: Epi-Spec2State: Convolutional state space model via spectrogram image sequences for prediction-oriented seizure state classification in EEG signals.
papers.summary: This paper presents Epi-Spec2State, a convolutional state space model that processes EEG spectrogram image sequences for prediction-oriented seizure state classification. It achieved 96.40%-96.60% accuracy and 98.20%-98.30% specificity on a private SEEG dataset, outperforming nine state-of-the-art methods on public datasets.

papers.title: An EEG-based fatigue detection framework integrating interpretable feature selection and efficient temporal modeling.
papers.summary: This paper introduces AXELLSTM, a cross-subject EEG-based fatigue detection framework with interpretable feature selection and efficient temporal modeling. It achieved 0.7454 accuracy and 0.7143 Macro-F1 under leave-one-subject-out validation, identifying 18 stable EEG channels and 8 key features.

papers.title: A Novel Adversarial Approach for EEG Dataset Refinement: Enhancing Generalization Through Proximity-to-Boundary Scoring.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a novel adversarial training framework that uses a proximity-to-boundary score to reduce the influence of noisy samples in EEG datasets, improving generalization. It achieved performance improvements up to 6.66% on motor imagery and 2.85% on sleep stage classification datasets.

papers.title: Parent and child-reported acceptability and preference of pediatric home sleep apnea testing versus In-lab polysomnography: a pilot study.
papers.summary: This pilot study assessed parent and child acceptability and preference for pediatric home sleep apnea testing (HSAT) versus in-lab polysomnography (PSG) in 15 children. HSAT was feasible and preferred by 60% of parents but only 33% of children, with sensor adjustments frequently required.

papers.title: Aftereffects of 1-week chronic intermittent hypoxia on the jaw muscle electromyographic activities during sleep in young adult rats.
papers.summary: This study investigated the aftereffects of 1-week chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH) on jaw muscle activity during sleep in young adult rats. CIH increased FosB expression in trigeminal premotor regions and noradrenergic innervation but selectively enhanced digastric muscle activity during arousal, without altering sleep architecture.

papers.title: "Early Stratification of Risk for Poor Neurological Outcome After Cardiac Arrest Is Improved with Processed EEG Data".
papers.summary: This study evaluated machine learning models using clinical data and processed EEG metrics (suppression ratio, bispectral index) to predict poor neurological outcome after cardiac arrest. Combining early EEG and clinical data significantly improved AUC to 0.88 for poor long-term outcome, outperforming either data source alone.

papers.title: Acute sleep deprivation rank-dependently enhances offensive aggression via the PVN in male mice.
papers.summary: This study found that acute sleep deprivation selectively enhances offensive aggression in dominant male mice but not subordinates, involving increased neuronal activation in the paraventricular nucleus (PVN). Chemogenetic inhibition of PVN neurons reversed this effect, linking sleep loss and social hierarchy to aggression via PVN.

papers.title: A Multi-Scale Adaptive EEG Feature Selection and Weighting Method for Mental Workload Estimation in Rapid Serial Visual Presentation.
papers.summary: The authors proposed a Multi-scale Adaptive Feature selection and Augmented Weighting (MAFA) framework for mental workload estimation in rapid serial visual presentation tasks. This method improved classification accuracy and revealed attention to posterior theta/alpha features, demonstrating feasibility and interpretability for RSVP-BCI systems.

papers.title: Physiologic and symptomatic burden across sleep-disordered breathing severity in men and women.
papers.summary: This study compared men and women matched on apnea-hypopnea index and other variables across sleep-disordered breathing severity. It found significant sex-by-severity interactions, with men showing more sleep fragmentation and sleepiness at moderate-to-severe severity, while women reported more insomnia symptoms and lower quality of life.

papers.title: CEREBROVASCULAR EVENTS AND NEUROCOGNITIVE IMPAIRMENTS WITH ALTERATIONS IN POLYSOMNOGRAPHIC INDICATORS FOLLOWING CARDIAC SURGERY.
papers.summary: This prospective study evaluated polysomnographic changes and neurocognitive outcomes after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass in 104 patients. Postoperative sleep alterations correlated with cognitive impairment, and Citicoline improved MoCA scores and sleep stabilization by day 30.

papers.title: Environmental enrichment attenuates chronic stress-induced disruptions in the gut microbiota, intestinal barrier, and brain.
papers.summary: This study investigated the effects of environmental enrichment (EE) on depressive-like behavior, gut microbiota, and intestinal barrier function in a chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) mouse model. EE attenuated stress-induced behavioral changes and partially reversed CUMS-induced alterations in microbial diversity and intestinal inflammation, suggesting EE as a non-pharmacological intervention for stabilizing the microbiota-gut-brain axis.

papers.title: Sleep and psychosis: An integrative review of conceptual and neurophysiological associations.
papers.summary: This review summarizes conceptual and neurophysiological associations between sleep processes (e.g., dreaming, insomnia) and psychosis. It highlights overlaps in anterior cingulate and frontal regions but notes that neurobiological evidence directly linking sleep to psychosis remains limited, identifying gaps for future research.

papers.title: Associations of Plasma Total Tau Level and MMSE Score With Polysomnographic Data in Middle-Aged Men With Severe Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Pilot Study.
papers.summary: In middle-aged men with severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), plasma total tau levels were negatively correlated with deep sleep duration and mean oxygen saturation, and positively correlated with apnea-hypopnea index, oxygen desaturation index, and arousal index. MMSE scores were negatively correlated with these OSA severity metrics, linking sleep fragmentation and hypoxia to cognitive impairment and neurodegeneration.

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Functional Connectivity and Independent Correlates of Cognitive Impairment in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation.
papers.summary: In patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and cognitive impairment, resting-state EEG showed reduced alpha-band functional connectivity compared to controls. Alpha-band wPLI was independently associated with cognitive impairment, suggesting its potential as an objective marker for AF-related cognitive decline.

papers.title: Nocturnal heart rate variability in Parkinson's disease: associations with autonomic dysfunction, cognitive function, and mood symptoms.
papers.summary: Nocturnal heart rate variability in Parkinson's disease (PD) revealed reduced sympathetic influence (lower LF, LF/HF) and higher parasympathetic activity (higher HF) compared to controls. In PD, stronger parasympathetic influence correlated with better cognitive performance, while subjective autonomic symptoms correlated with poorer cognition and mood.

papers.title: Association Between Nocturnal Oxygen Desaturation and the Severity of Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Retrospective Study.
papers.summary: This retrospective single-center study investigated associations between apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) and nocturnal oxygenation parameters in obstructive sleep apnea patients. AHI was positively correlated with oxygen desaturation index and T90, and inversely with minimum and mean nocturnal SpO2, with all Holm-adjusted p-values <0.001.

papers.title: Negative BOLD response to interictal discharges in epilepsy using intracranial EEG-fMRI.
authors: the, Calgary Comprehensive Epilepsy Program collaborators
papers.summary: This study used intracranial EEG-fMRI to examine spatial relationships between positive and negative BOLD responses to interictal epileptiform discharges in drug-resistant focal epilepsy. Positive BOLD clusters were significantly closer to epileptogenic tissue than negative clusters, whereas negative clusters showed greater overlap with the default mode network, supporting prioritization of positive BOLD for presurgical evaluation.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture improves neurocognitive impairment induced by chronic sleep deprivation: an experimental study based on hippocampal neurogenesis and synaptic plasticity.
papers.summary: This experimental study in male Wistar rats examined whether electroacupuncture at cervical acupoints improves cognitive impairment induced by chronic sleep deprivation. It found that electroacupuncture enhanced learning and memory and reversed abnormalities in hippocampal neurogenesis and synaptic plasticity.

papers.title: Association between habitual sleep duration and Alzheimer's disease: A cross-sectional study based on NHANES 2007-2018.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study using NHANES 2007-2018 data found a significant positive association between longer habitual sleep duration and Alzheimer's disease prevalence in US adults. The association persisted after adjustment and across subgroups, suggesting sleep duration as a potential predictive tool for AD.

papers.title: Adolescent depression recognition and symptom prediction based on multi-view EEG network: an exploratory study.
papers.summary: This exploratory study compared a Multi-view Adaptive Graph Convolutional Network (MVA-GCN) based on resting-state EEG with traditional questionnaires for diagnosing adolescent depression. The MVA-GCN achieved 99.84% accuracy in classification, with occipital and fronto-central regions contributing most, but findings on brain-resilience associations were not significant after correction.

papers.title: From bench to bedside: current evidence and prospects for acupuncture in managing perioperative neurocognitive disorders.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on acupuncture's mechanisms and clinical value for perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND), proposing that electroacupuncture and transcutaneous acupoint stimulation counteract multiple risk pathways via gut-brain axis modulation and multi-target neuroprotection, reducing PND incidence and accelerating cognitive recovery. The review highlights the interaction of perioperative risk factors and acupuncture's coordinated neuroprotective network.

papers.title: Armillariella tabescens polysaccharide targets microglial glycolysis to alleviate sleep deprivation-induced neuroinflammation through the mTOR signaling pathway.
papers.summary: This study isolated a polysaccharide (ATEP) from Armillariella tabescens and showed in mouse and cell models that it alleviates sleep deprivation-induced neuroinflammation by inhibiting mTOR signaling, correcting glycolytic reprogramming, and promoting microglial M2 polarization. ATEP improved cognitive function, reduced neurotoxic proteins, and preserved synaptic integrity.

papers.title: Cross-Sectional Associations of Insomnia, Social Dysfunction, Suicidality, and Depressive Symptoms in Rural Adults with Schizophrenia: A Sex-Stratified Analysis.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 931 rural adults with schizophrenia found that insomnia, social dysfunction, suicidality, and depressive symptoms were positively associated, with women reporting higher scores. Exploratory analyses suggested indirect associations of insomnia with depressive symptoms via social dysfunction and suicidality, but not serially, and sex did not moderate these associations.

papers.title: Cardiac Autonomic Modulation in Seizure Disorders With and Without Interictal Epileptiform Discharges: A Retrospective Heart Rate Variability Analysis Using Archived Digital EEG Recordings.
papers.summary: This retrospective study analyzed heart rate variability (HRV) from archived EEG recordings in 45 adults and found that patients with seizure disorders had lower vagally mediated HRV than a non-seizure neurological comparison group, but the presence of interictal epileptiform discharges did not add measurable alterations. No significant differences in HRV were found between the two seizure groups.

papers.title: Cenobamate and Trazodone Combination Suppresses Seizures, EEG Alterations, Preserves Neuronal Architecture and Normalizes the BDNF/TrkB Expression in PTZ‑Kindled Mice.
papers.summary: This study in PTZ-kindled mice found that combination therapy with cenobamate and trazodone suppressed seizures, normalized EEG alterations, preserved hippocampal neuronal architecture, and restored BDNF/TrkB expression, whereas monotherapies did not. The combination showed additive effects on reducing hyperexcitability and neuropathology.

papers.title: Evaluation of tirzepatide as an adjunct to buprenorphine for the treatment of opioid use disorder (TAB) trial: study design and rationale.
papers.summary: This paper describes the design and rationale of the TAB trial, a randomized controlled trial testing tirzepatide as an adjunct to buprenorphine for opioid use disorder, with primary outcome of 6-month buprenorphine retention.

papers.title: Multidomain perioperative physiological vulnerability, longitudinal recovery patterns, and clinical outcomes after gastrointestinal cancer surgery in older adults.
papers.summary: This prospective cohort study of older adults undergoing gastrointestinal cancer surgery developed a Perioperative Aging Burden Index (PABI) integrating multidomain physiological assessments. Higher PABI was associated with increased postoperative delirium, complications, delayed discharge, and poorer disease-free and overall survival.

papers.title: Associations of sleep duration variability and depressive symptoms with gastrointestinal disease among middle-aged and older adults: A cohort study.
papers.summary: This cohort study using CHARLS and HRS data found that greater variability in sleep duration was associated with increased risk of gastrointestinal disease, with depressive symptoms partially mediating this association.

papers.title: Transcranial direct current stimulation enhances cognitive performance and modulates QEEG beta- and theta-band power in patients undergoing whole-brain radiotherapy.
papers.summary: This randomized sham-controlled trial found that transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) improved cognitive performance and reduced QEEG beta and theta power in patients undergoing whole-brain radiotherapy, suggesting a potential neuroprotective effect.

papers.title: Interplay of patent foramen ovale and atrial septum aneurysm in a nonagenarian patient presenting with platypnoea-orthodeoxia syndrome.
papers.summary: This case report describes a nonagenarian with patent foramen ovale and atrial septal aneurysm presenting with platypnoea-orthodeoxia syndrome, successfully treated with percutaneous PFO closure.
